seven_conditional_fact_reviews.independent_assessment: Q denotes incoming RDI copied to RBX; T denotes incoming RSI copied to R14 before the first opaque direct call. These are symbolic carriers.
qualifications: No object/class/constructor/allocator/ABI or parameter identity inferred. Subsequent carrier use assumes each opaque call returns normally preserving RBX/R14 and an intact stack.

seven_conditional_fact_reviews.independent_assessment: LEA computes 0x106cb7258; ADD 0x10 produces 0x106cb7268; the resulting 64-bit address is stored through the RBX carrier.
qualifications: Address computation is not a read of the addressed global bytes. The store establishes no vtable/type/class/constructor/processor role. Valid writable destination and noninterference are premises.

seven_conditional_fact_reviews.independent_assessment: At the first selected call frontier RDI carries Q+0x48 and the low scalar in XMM0 comes from signed32-to-single conversion of a load through T. At the second, RDI carries Q+0x118, XMM0 is converted from a second T load, and the loaded 32-bit memory value at 0x105db97cc is in the low lane of XMM1 and copied by MOVAPS to XMM2.
qualifications: Callees and global bytes remain unread. These are machine-register call-frontier facts, not proven ABI signatures or public parameter units. The two loads through T need not match after intervening writes. No numeric constant, rounding law, complete upper-lane invariant or behavior of either callee is established. Malformed SSE ESIL strings were not used.

seven_conditional_fact_reviews.independent_assessment: Nine literal calls target 0x101b2b930, each preceded by a LEA carrying the listed Q-relative address in RDI.
qualifications: The first LEA at 0x102247d99 is separated from its call at 0x102247daa by the dword store at 0x102247da0; no adjacency assumption is required. All nine helper bodies, writes, write extents, return values and roles remain unknown. The spacing of carriers does not prove element size, layout, count of initialized objects or a 20-byte write. No ARM-side rule is imported.

seven_conditional_fact_reviews.independent_assessment: The selected instructions support the exact local write operations and widths; they do not prove surviving object defaults.

byte_evidence.load: opaque 64-bit memory bits at 0x105a781b0 to XMM0

qualifications: Earlier writes can be changed by opaque calls or aliasing. The dword at Q+0x15f overlaps the last byte of the preceding qword at Q+0x158 and extends through Q+0x162; do not treat them as disjoint fields. No numeric meaning for global bits, portable layout, final zero/default invariant or helper write boundary follows.

seven_conditional_fact_reviews.independent_assessment: After all nine calls, RAX is loaded from qword [T+0x10]. Let L denote this late value. The local subsequent stores do not change RAX, and the ordinary epilogue RET therefore returns L under the stated normal-flow and stack/memory premises.

byte_evidence.effect: RET; RAX not otherwise changed after the late load

qualifications: L is not proved zero, Q, an earlier helper result, a processor/model pointer or an accepted public return law. Opaque helpers and concurrent/aliasing writes can affect the memory read at this late time. Final memory survival and actual return assume valid memory, ordinary call returns, no intervening external writes, and destinations that do not corrupt the saved registers/return address or other required stack state.

seven_conditional_fact_reviews.independent_assessment: The selected physical suffix contains EB00 to the immediately following address, register-carrier moves, two further direct calls, and a final 15-byte NOP. It is beyond the earlier RET and is not reached by that ordinary fall-through path.
qualifications: No entry or path into this suffix, exception/unwind/destructor/cleanup role, termination law or callee behavior is established. RBX at a hypothetical suffix entry is only a register carrier; the preceding epilogue restored it, so the suffix is not a proof that Q is passed. R14 preservation across its opaque first call is a further premise for passing the saved incoming RAX value onward. The retained ESIL target 0x102287e5e is inconsistent with raw PC+2+0 and agreeing opcode/jump 0x102247e5e; all ESIL is excluded.
